title: SsvcPolicy
description: How the tenant makes its CISA SSVC decision (https://www.cisa.gov/stakeholder-specific-vulnerability-categorization-ssvc) for a finding: Track, Track*, Attend or Act. The decision table is the CISA Coordinator table 2.0.3 and is fixed: four decision points (exploitation, automatable, technical impact, mission and well-being) go in. This document configures how Vulnetix's signals become those four values (CEL over the finding variables, and the repository's criticality for mission and well-being), which table cells the organisation reads differently (mapping), which findings it decides by rule instead (overrides), and what each outcome asks of it (outcomes). A field left out takes the default, which is the policy of a tenant with no document. One per tenant.

exploitation.description: When a finding counts as exploited. Active wins when both conditions hold; when neither does, exploitation is none.

active.description: Credible evidence of exploitation in the wild. CEL over the finding variables.

poc.description: A public proof of concept or a well-known method exists. CEL over the finding variables.

automatable.description: Holds when an attacker can reliably automate steps 1 to 4 of the kill chain (reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation) for the finding. CEL over the finding variables.

technicalImpact.description: Holds when exploiting the finding gives total control of the software or total disclosure of its information; otherwise the impact is partial. CEL over the finding variables.

missionWellBeing.description: The mission and well-being value of a finding in a repository, by the repository's criticality (RepositorySettings spec.criticality). unclassified is a repository with no criticality.

mapping.description: Reads cells of the decision table differently. A rule matches every cell whose decision points are among the values it lists; a decision point it leaves out matches any value. When several rules match a cell, the last one wins. A rule changes a cell for the whole tenant: to decide by a property of the finding or its repository, use overrides.

overrides.description: Decides the findings a condition holds for by rule, after the table and the mapping. The first rule that holds sets the outcome, so list the most specific first.

name.description: Shown beside the decision when this rule set it.

when.description: CEL over the finding variables, including the repository's labels, owner and criticality.

outcomes.description: What each outcome asks of the organisation. The priority is what a finding with that outcome is ranked as; dueDays is its remediation window, and 0 or left out means the standard update cycle.

missionValue.description: Mission and well-being: the combination of mission prevalence and public well-being impact.

outcome.description: The SSVC decision. Track and Track* are remediated in the standard update cycle (Track* is watched more closely), Attend sooner, Act as soon as possible.

priority.description: low, medium, high or immediate. Defaults: Track low, Track* medium, Attend high, Act immediate.

dueDays.description: The remediation window in days. 0 or left out is the standard update cycle.
